fields.title: Product strategy: a sequence of choices, not a wishlist
fields.keyTakeaway: Strategy answers where we play and how we win, and explicitly names what we will not do. A document that doesn't make it clear what you gave up is not a strategy.
fields.checkQuestion: The strategy says "become the best reading product." What is missing?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key question of the node: **which decisions realize the vision?**
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **Where we play** — segments, situations, geography. Always specifying where we do not play.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **How we win** — what we do better and why it is hard to replicate.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **How it's configured** — what capabilities and resources are needed: data, channel, partnerships, team.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **What sequence** — what we do this year, what opens up only afterwards, what we give up now to make it possible.
fields.blocks/2/text: **Marketing mix (7Ps)** is useful as a completeness check: product, price, place, promotion, people, process, physical evidence. A strategy that only thinks through the product part usually stumbles on price or lack of sales capacity.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Where we play: people who want to read but don't finish. Where we don't play: heavy readers who need a huge catalog and rare editions.

How we win: getting them through their first book — curation, pace, reminders at the right moment. Huge catalogs don't have this and won't make it a priority.

What is needed: data on where exactly people drop off (have it), editorial work on recommendations (hiring), publisher partnerships for short formats (don't have, starting negotiations).

What we give up: chasing catalog size and buying rights to new releases at any price.

Sequence: year one — finishing books; year two — social reading built on that reputation.
fields.blocks/4/text: Resources are finite, so winning in one place usually means agreeing to concede in another. If a document contains no trade-offs, decisions will be made from scratch every time based on circumstances.
fields.blocks/4/title: "We want to be the best at everything" is an absence of strategy
fields.blocks/5/text: Strategy is not a forecast. It sets the direction and decision-making rules; specific moves will change every quarter, and that's normal as long as the answers to the four questions above remain unchanged.
